chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said:

I said to Abi Ja'far عليه السلام: What suffices of speech in the last two rak'ahs? He said: That you say, “Subhan Allah, wal-hamdu lillah, wa la ilaha illa Allah, wa Allahu akbar,” then you pronounce takbir and bow.

key_terms.الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ الْأَخِيرَتَيْنِ: the final two units of a four-rak'ah prayer
key_terms.الْقَوْلِ: the verbal recitation to be said in prayer
key_terms.سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ: glory be to Allah; a formula of tasbih
key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: there is no god but Allah
key_terms.يُجْزِي: is sufficient or fulfills the required minimum

ai.seo_question: What is sufficient to recite in the last two rak'ahs of salat according to Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states what is sufficient to say in the final two rak'ahs of salat. Imam Abi Ja'far عليه السلام teaches that tasbih in the form of the four phrases of glorification and praise suffices, after which one says takbir and performs ruku'.
